title: Augment token contrast engine and modal focus rehydration for dense widgets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview: We need to improve how our color token matrix is evaluated for compact/dense components (tables, compact charts, condensed buttons) and simultaneously ensure modal and popover focus behavior reliably restores and rehydrates focus across screen readers and zoom magnifiers. This ticket pairs a tokens-level contrast re-evaluation with a UX fix for focus restoration when modals close in dense UI contexts.

Problem statement: Several customer audits and internal QA found where compact variants render text and controls at sizes or densities that fall below perceptual contrast thresholds (esp. shadows/pinned disabled states), and modals/popovers used in dense lists do not consistently return focus to the triggering cell on VoiceOver/NVDA when the page has virtualized DOMs or when zoom is enabled. These issues increase VPAT risk and are a source of several support escalations.

Scope:
- Re-run contrast evaluation for compact token palette (text-on-surface, icons-on-control, disabled-contrast mapping) and create a contrast matrix with recommended token deltas.
- Update token recommendation guidance and produce a compatibility layer for components to opt-in to "dense-contrast" tokens.
- Implement a focus rehydration strategy for modal/popover close that works with virtualized lists and preserves scroll position; include keyboard nav flows and screen reader announce changes.
- Provide a VPAT addendum describing the changes and testing notes.

Out of scope: Full theme redesign, runtime feature flags for A/B rollout (will be separate ENG task).

Acceptance criteria and test plan are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Contrast matrix published: every compact token pair has computed contrast ratio with WCAG 2.1 offsets documented (CSV attached)
All updated compact tokens meet at least 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large/bold text where used; exceptions must be documented with compensating techniques
Design tokens provided as JSON patch and documented in the design tokens registry with migration notes
Modal/popover close restores focus to the originating interactive element in 3 major browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) with VoiceOver and NVDA tested and recorded
Focus rehydration works with virtualized lists (example: table virtual scroll) without losing keyboard navigation order or breaking skip-links
Engineering PR with tests + accessibility e2e harness (axe + NVDA smoke script) linked and passing in CI
VPAT addendum drafted and reviewed by Accessibility SME and Legal reviewer
comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha: Kickoff: ran initial token audit against compact palette. Found 12 token pairs below 4.5:1 when rendered at 13px in high-density tables. Filed sample screenshots in Confluence.

2025-02-25 - Marco: Prototyped dense-contrast token namespace (token.dense.*). Shared Figma patches for table row, compact button, and small chart legend. Needs engineering viability check for theme merge.

2025-02-28 - Eng review (Sara Iqbal): Kernel decision: prefer CSS custom property layer with fallback rather than runtime token swap to avoid re-render penalties. ENG-24321 created to implement utility variables.
2025-03-03 - PM (Liam Ortiz): Confirming customer impact cases and prioritization. Agreed to include VPAT note for upcoming release window.

2025-03-07 - Accessibility review (Danielle Park): Modal focus rehydration approach looked good; recommended adding a delayed focus restoration path for zoom+screen-magnifier scenarios. Added NVDA repro steps.

2025-03-10 - Marco: Implemented prototype focus rehydration using an inert+aria-hidden pattern and a small 'focus-sentinel' on close. Created PR #1218. Unit tests added for focus restoration in jest-dom.
2025-03-12 - Aisha: Design verification pass complete for buttons and table rows. Two remaining contrast diffs for disabled chips noted; flagged for trade-off discussion.
decisions: Adopt 'token.dense.*' namespaced tokens and leave default tokens unchanged to minimize breaking changes for existing customers
Use CSS custom properties evaluated at the component root to allow component-level opt-in rather than global theme swap
Focus restore will prefer a non-invasive sentinel element approach over aggressive tabindex juggling to reduce unexpected side effects in virtualized lists
Document exceptions where 4.5:1 is impractical (tiny icon glyphs) and ship compensating UX (focus rings, increased target size)
